findings.where: Intro, the three numbered points under the lead paragraph ("No hostel can pay for a higher position" and the other two)
findings.fault: These three lines are the whole promise of the page, but they are set like ordinary body text. When you squint at the page, the H1 and the large lead paragraph stand out, then the section headings. The three points don't stand out at all. Nothing groups them as a summary either, such as a shared panel, a label or a change of size, so they look like the start of the prose rather than the takeaway.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker who arrives from a listing to check whether the ranking can be trusted, usually on a phone. They want the answer in a few seconds, but it reads as one more paragraph, so they either leave without it or have to read the long sections to find it.

findings.where: "Ranking method" section, its four paragraphs (worst on phone, where it runs about three screens with no break)
findings.fault: One heading covers four different topics: payment cannot buy rank, scores are pulled toward the area average, every review counts toward the score, and the default sort and filters. There is no subhead or visual break between them. The section after it, "Scoring method", is one short paragraph and a list, even though the area-average paragraph is really about scoring. The sections are badly unbalanced and the long one is a wall of text.
findings.who_objects: A visitor looking for one specific answer, such as "why does this hostel with 3 reviews score so well?". They have no way to jump to it and have to read about 450 words of undivided prose. On a phone in transit, many will stop reading.

findings.where: End of the page, after "Hostelworld, for comparison" (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The page stops at the comparison paragraph and goes straight into the footer. There is no next step, such as a link to Destinations, anywhere in the content. The only way onward is the nav or the footer links.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who now trusts the ranking and wants to go back to choosing a hostel. The page gives them nowhere to go at the moment they are convinced, so they have to scroll back up to the nav.

findings.where: Whole page at 1440 px: the content column against the nav and footer
findings.fault: The text runs in a narrow column pinned to the left edge, under the wordmark, and the right 55–60% of every screen is empty sand. The footer below is centred. The page reads lopsided, as if a sidebar failed to load. The left-aligned column and the centred footer also break the page's continuity.
findings.who_objects: A desktop visitor planning their next stop. The half-empty, unbalanced screen looks unfinished, which works against a page that exists to show care and rigour.

findings.where: Intro list of three points, and the decay list in "Scoring method" (100% / 50% / 25%)
findings.fault: Both use the same numbered-list style, so by similarity they read as the same kind of thing. The intro points are unordered principles, yet the numbers 1–3 suggest steps. In the decay list, the counters 1–3 sit next to the percentages and compete with the figures the reader actually needs.
findings.who_objects: A careful reader comparing the decay rates. The extra numbers slow the scan, and the numbered principles imply an order that doesn't exist.

findings.fault: The links wrap after "How we rank" and leave a "·" separator hanging at the end of the first line. The second line, "Report content · luc@…", then starts without one. The row looks broken.
findings.who_objects: A phone visitor who scrolls to the footer looking for contact or legal links. The stray separator looks like a rendering slip on a page that asks for trust.
